title: KMP String Matching
problem: A genetic researcher is aligning a long DNA strand text and needs to quickly find the first occurrence position of the target gene probe pattern. Return -1 if not found, or 0 if pattern is an empty string. You can build a prefix table by analyzing the repetitive structure of the pattern itself, achieving smart jumps during matching and avoiding character-by-character matching from the beginning.
strategy: Use the KMP prefix table; the trace only records key steps such as initialization, one prefix table update, one mismatch backtracking, and one successful match, without unrolling the entire loop character by character.
learning_objectives: Master the construction process of the prefix table pi in the KMP algorithm and its role in backtracking the j pointer upon mismatch
Understand the pointer state changes of text and pattern during matching, and be able to predict the next operation based on the current state
Be able to identify invariants in the matching process, such as the length of the matched prefix always equal to j

interaction_tasks.feedback_correct: Correct! j backtracks to 0, then the next comparison is made.
interaction_tasks.feedback_wrong: Observe the value of pi[j-1]; upon mismatch, j should backtrack to the position of pi[j-1].
interaction_tasks.oracle: According to the move event of this step in the trace, check whether j becomes pi[1]=0, and in the next frame i remains 3 and j is 0.
interaction_tasks.prompt: When text="ababc", pattern="abc", currently i=3, j=2 and pattern[2]='c' mismatches with text[3]='b', and pi[1]=0, what is the next state? (Hint: how will the j pointer change?)
interaction_tasks.stage2_affordance: Drag the j pointer slider to visualize the backtracking process.

interaction_tasks.feedback_correct: Correct! This is the invariant of the partial match.
interaction_tasks.feedback_wrong: Check whether the substring in text from i-j to i-1 equals the first j characters of pattern.
interaction_tasks.oracle: The answer should be B, which can be verified by checking whether the slice of text in the current state matches the first j characters of pattern.
interaction_tasks.prompt: At any moment in the KMP matching process, what invariant relationship exists between the matched prefix length j and the index i? Please select: A) i always equals j; B) text[i-j...i-1] is equal to pattern[0...j-1]; C) pattern[0...i] equals text.
interaction_tasks.stage2_affordance: Highlight the comparison between the substring text[i-j:i] and pattern[0:j].

interaction_tasks.stage2_affordance: Provide a text box to directly modify pattern and update the prefix table and matching animation in real time.
